text.title: Agency Risk Register Template — Worked Example
text.summary: One complete Monday register for a six-person studio (28-minute refresh, concentration recomputed from the 90-day billing export with Client A at 47 percent scored 20 and mitigated by Friday, seven rows across the six classes with dated key-person remediation, currency shares, a tested contractor, 3.5 months of pipeline coverage and a GDPR row, one closed row with its lesson) with a note per value, plus a Wednesday 60-minute register full of project rows and estimates and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: Brightline Studio is a six-person design and build agency. Dana Kovac, the founder, holds a 30-minute slot every Monday. The trailing-90-day billing export on 2026-09-14 shows Client A at 47 percent of revenue and Client B at 22 percent; 60 percent of revenue is billed in USD while 90 percent of costs are in EUR; Marko alone holds the AWS root credentials; one contractor works from Portugal; the CRM's stage-weighted pipeline is 210,000 against a 60,000 monthly cost base; two GDPR processor agreements are unsigned.

example.title: Brightline Studio, Monday 2026-09-14
example.note: All six agency classes have a row and no project row is present; the closed tab holds the registrar-credential row with its lesson rather than a deletion (r-six-agency-risk-classes, r-closed-tab-not-delete). Every row carries the 8 columns, Dana or Priya as owner and a trigger that a Monday scan can check: two missed invoices, five working days of absence, a 5 percent currency move, coverage under 3 months (r-eight-column-row). Concentration comes from the billing export over 90 days recomputed on the refresh date; Client A at 47 percent is scored 4 x 5 = 20, above the automatic 15 floor for a client at 40 percent or more, and Client B at 22 percent has its own row (r-concentration-90d-auto-score). The key-person row names the credentials, the holder, Priya as remediation owner and 2026-09-30 as the hand-over date (r-key-person-bus-factor-dated). The FX row prints 60/40 revenue against 90/10 costs by currency, and the contractor row names Portugal, the control-and-substitution test and its outcome (r-cross-border-rows-quantified). 210,000 over 60,000 is 3.5 months of coverage with the trigger at 3 (r-pipeline-months-of-coverage). The refresh ran 5 + 15 + 8 = 28 minutes with no overrun (r-thirty-minute-monday). The only row at 15 or more, R-01, carries a mitigation owned by Dana and due on Friday of the refresh week; the FX row at 12 needs no response yet (r-score-15-action-or-signed-acceptance).

example.title: a Wednesday hour of project rows and estimates
example.note: What the validator prints: `rows` lacks contractor_classification and regulatory rows, and P-17 and P-18 carry ids and classes outside the register (r-six-agency-risk-classes); `concentration.source` must be billing_export and `trailing_days` 90 (r-concentration-90d-auto-score); R-01 has owner "team" and R-02 owner "ops", triggers "if things get worse" and "someone leaves" are too short to be observable, and R-01 at 18 has `response` null (r-eight-column-row, r-score-15-action-or-signed-acceptance); R-02 lacks `remediation_owner` and `deadline` (r-key-person-bus-factor-dated); R-03 lacks `revenue_share_by_currency` and `cost_share_by_currency` (r-cross-border-rows-quantified); with `consecutive_overruns` 2, `split_or_prune_required` must be true (r-thirty-minute-monday). Once the schema violations are fixed the cross-field checks add: 2026-09-16 is not a Monday and 60 minutes is not 10 + 45 + 20 nor inside the timebox; the recompute date is June; Client A's row says 30 percent where the export says 47 and 18 is not 4 x 5; and 4 months of coverage is not 120,000 over 60,000.
